title: Per-component order and duplicate independence for Cedar's isAuthorized
intent: The head theorem `order_and_dup_independent` shows that Cedar's authorizer response does not depend on policy order or duplicates. It is proved component-wise: one lemma each for the forbid-satisfied, permit-satisfied and erroring components of `isAuthorized`, and the glue reassembles `isAuthorized` from the three equalities in a single `simp`.

parent.name: order_and_dup_independent
parent.statement:
theorem order_and_dup_independent (request : Request) (entities : Entities) (policies₁ policies₂ : Policies) :
  policies₁ ≡ policies₂ →
  isAuthorized request entities policies₁ = isAuthorized request entities policies₂

children.name: satisfiedPolicies_order_and_dup_independent
children.statement:
theorem satisfiedPolicies_order_and_dup_independent {policies₁ policies₂ : Policies} (effect : Effect) (request : Request) (entities : Entities) :
  policies₁ ≡ policies₂ →
  satisfiedPolicies effect policies₁ request entities = satisfiedPolicies effect policies₂ request entities
children.closed_by: exact List.filterMap_equiv (satisfiedWithEffect effect · request entities) policies₁ policies₂ h₁
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: satisfiedPolicies effect is order/dup independent: an order/dup-equivalent policies list yields the same set of satisfied policy ids, for either effect

children.name: errorPolicies_order_and_dup_independent
children.statement:
theorem errorPolicies_order_and_dup_independent {policies₁ policies₂ : Policies} (request : Request) (entities : Entities) :
  policies₁ ≡ policies₂ →
  errorPolicies policies₁ request entities = errorPolicies policies₂ request entities
children.closed_by: exact List.filterMap_equiv (errored · request entities) policies₁ policies₂ h₁
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: errorPolicies is order/dup independent: an order/dup-equivalent policies list yields the same set of erroring policy ids

applicability.goal_shape: An equality `f x = f y` (or a congruence) for a composite function `f` built as a `let`-bound/branching combination of a fixed set of named components; here `f = isAuthorized`, a combination of `satisfiedPolicies .forbid`, `satisfiedPolicies .permit` and `errorPolicies`.
applicability.use_when: the composite is generated from a fixed structure, so per-component lemmas mirror it one-to-one; each component is itself `Set.make (policies.filterMap g)`, so its invariance reduces to a single `List.filterMap_equiv` rewrite; the glue then closes with one `simp [f, h₁ … hₙ]`.
applicability.avoid_when: the composite's body reads anything other than its components — the raw policies list directly, or an argument the per-component lemmas do not hold equal — because the per-component equalities only licence rewriting the components, and a body that depends on something else cannot be closed by the simp. (Branching on the components themselves is fine: isAuthorized branches on forbids.isEmpty && !permits.isEmpty yet the simp still closes, since any property of a component is preserved by component equality.) Avoid it too when the components do not share one lemma shape, so each needs a distinct argument rather than a template.

claims.claim: The theorem `order_and_dup_independent` is declared in `cedar-lean/Cedar/Thm/Authorization.lean` lines 158-166.

The glue assembles 2 direct lemmas in a 9-line proof — `satisfiedPolicies_order_and_dup_independent` applied twice (for `.forbid` and `.permit`) and `errorPolicies_order_and_dup_independent` once — while each child proof is 8 lines and the project-lemma chain below the theorem runs 3 deep (child → `Set.make_make_eqv` → `List.canonicalize_equiv`), counted from the site line ranges and by reading the two child proofs.
claims.evidence: site ranges in the copied files: parent cedar-lean/Cedar/Thm/Authorization.lean lines 158-166 (9 lines), children cedar-lean/Cedar/Thm/Authorization/Authorizer.lean lines 62-69 and 71-78 (8 lines each); both child proofs rewrite by Set.make_make_eqv then exact List.filterMap_equiv, and Set.make_make_eqv's proof (https://github.com/cedar-policy/cedar-spec/blob/e619491a5bfb04970ef994dbe286df0bb9d0b73f/cedar-lean/Cedar/Thm/Data/Set.lean#L303-L318) calls List.canonicalize_equiv (https://github.com/cedar-policy/cedar-spec/blob/e619491a5bfb04970ef994dbe286df0bb9d0b73f/cedar-lean/Cedar/Thm/Data/List/Canonical.lean#L468-L480).

claims.claim: The same component-wise move appears a second time in the same file: `satisfied_policies_congr_evaluate` (lines 80-89) and `error_policies_congr_evaluate` (lines 91-102) prove the same two components congr under evaluation, combined by `is_authorized_congr_evaluate` (lines 117-126) with the same `simp only [isAuthorized, …]` glue.

metrics.how_counted: line spans of the parent and child sites, declaration included

consequences: One lemma per component of `isAuthorized`, so the obligations are: (1) every component must be covered — the glue applies `satisfiedPolicies_order_and_dup_independent` twice, once per effect, and `errorPolicies_order_and_dup_independent` once, and missing one component leaves the final `simp` unable to close; (2) each component's definition must be of the shape `Set.make (policies.filterMap g)`, or the `unfold`/`rw [Set.make_make_eqv]`/`exact List.filterMap_equiv` template does not apply; (3) the glue's `simp [isAuthorized, hf, hp, he]` only closes because `isAuthorized` is literally a combination of the three components, so a change to `isAuthorized`'s body that branches on more than set-equality breaks the glue. Failure mode: the two per-component lemmas are near-identical templates, so a change to the shared `Set.make`/`filterMap` infrastructure breaks the whole family at once.

generality objection: reworded avoid_when so it no longer says to avoid branching on the contents/size of the components (isAuthorized branches on forbids.isEmpty && !permits.isEmpty and still closes); it now says the body must depend only on the components and fails when it reads anything outside the per-component equalities
